newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO DISSOLVES VVA AGENCY, GOVERNMENT ABSORBS.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO DISSOLVES VVA AGENCY, GOVERNMENT ABSORBS.

text.p: Mexico on Monday said it was dissolving the VVA agency charged with selling distressed assets to stave off bankruptcy in the banking sector after the 1994-95 peso crisis.

"The Bank's Fund for the Protection of Savings (FOBAPROA)...is taking over the sale functions that VVA (Valuation and Sale of Assets) has carried out until today," the statement said, adding the decision was made so as to concentrate the process of recovering the value of distressed assets into a single body.
FOBAPROA, the government's bank bail-out fund, said in the statement that it would take over VVA's activities.

"While VVA will continue initially as an independent organisation, from today all its activities will start to operate as a single body. Later all VVA's activities will be incorporated in a formal way into FOBAPROA," it said.

FOBAPROA took some 340 billion pesos ($43.2 billion) -- equivalent to 13.36 percent of Mexico's gross domestic product -- off the hands of the crisis-hit banks and onto its books as interest rates soared and revenues plunged after the December 1994 peso crash.
